key_insight: Digital motor scores from wearables map onto specific striatal dopamine deficits in Parkinson’s disease, especially for gait, with added frontostriatal network changes.
clinical_relevance: Digital health measures may help characterize distinct PD motor domains and could support more precise biomarker development for tracking disease-related motor dysfunction.
method: 17 Parkinson’s patients and 39 healthy controls underwent simultaneous 11C-dMP PET and resting-state fMRI.
Researchers computed composite digital motor scores for arm swing, gait, and balance from digital health technology data.
Voxel-based PET correlations were linked to seed-based functional connectivity analyses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports domain-specific PET associations, with the strongest finding for gait showing lower dopamine transporter binding linked to worse scores in the right caudate and anteromedial putamen, plus reduced frontostriatal connectivity.
watch_item: Small sample size and cross-sectional design limit generalization and prevent conclusions about clinical utility or causality.
paper_title: Striatal representations and network correlates of digital motor scores in Parkinsons disease
